correctness.rationale: Writing N=max(E,F) with E Euclidean and F=lambda|x_1|, every numerator chooses one of four active-branch combinations. EE and FF satisfy Ptolemy with constant one (the latter after projection to the real line), while each mixed case is at most lambda times the Euclidean Ptolemy numerator because F<=lambda E. Hence C_Pt<=lambda. For x=(1/2,1/2), y=(1/2,-1/2), z=(1,0), the numerator is lambda and, exactly when lambda<=sqrt(2), all four denominator-side norms equal 1/sqrt(2), so the denominator is one and the ratio is lambda. The endpoint is valid because the two branches merely tie. This proves the stated full interval without numerical inference.
